name: Interpolation

blog.title: Interpolation Methods
blog.description: Five ways to draw a curve through the same set of points — linear, cubic spline, PCHIP, Akima, and FFT resampling — and what each one assumes about the data you didn't measure.

calculator.title: Online Interpolation Calculator, Multiple line, Vector, Matrix, Sheet type data, Fast calculation & Plot results (Graph)
calculator.description: Free interpolation calculator. Copy and paste CSV, TSV, or spreadsheet data, compute multiple lines and matrix data at once, and plot results. No upload.

advanced.title: Advanced Interpolation Calculator - Cubic Spline, PCHIP, Akima
advanced.description: Interpolate many series with cubic spline, PCHIP, or Akima. Paste CSV or TSV, set a range, plot the result. Your data is sent to the server to compute.
advanced.//methods: Static copy sits in the Method select. No FFT: it needs a uniform x grid.
advanced.//dataset: Two flat runs with sharp edges. Chosen because the four methods disagree by ~20% of the data range at x=3.5: cubic overshoots to 119.6 and dips to -13.6, Akima half that, PCHIP stays inside the data, linear ramps. The basic page's smooth demo hides all of that.
advanced.//range: Static copy sits in the three Output X inputs. 0-1000 is the basic page's; meaningless for 11 points spanning 0..10.

insight: Interpolation estimates an unknown value between two known points by assuming how the quantity behaves in between — the simplest assumption being a straight line.
//dataset: Demo data seeded into the input grid on first load. 50 points, x 0-1000.
